note: Adjudicated accidental variants: two of punctuation and one of accent. Substantive text agrees across the three complete witnesses with zero variants. The two punctuation rulings keep the comma the Benziger page prints before et at both places, where the Clementine Vulgate points them the same way; only witness do omits it.

adjudicated.ruling: Stress on the antepenult, with DO. Circumdo is a compound of do, dare, whose a is short, so the penult of circumdabo is short and cannot carry the stress; the hand missal's accent would have the reader say the word wrongly. Accents are the accidental class the collation strips before comparing letters (ORTHOGRAPHY.md), so the difference is adjudicated here rather than declared as a corrigendum in the witness.
The approved Benziger printing's punctuation is retained. The difference marks phrasing and does not change the words.
